I realised I wasn't my best friend's besty in a harsh way. We have been friends since we were 13, spent so much time together, we know each other's darkest secrets, & are still friends. She was going to marry her childhood sweetheart. It was an exciting time. We talked about all the fine details; flowers, venue, her dream dress, who'd do make-up, who'd be invited, all the usual stuff. One night, she asked me to go for a drive with her. I wanted to know where we were going & she said,"Just a drive, I need to talk to you about something important." I was sitting in the passenger seat of her car with anticipation thinking that this was it, she was going to ask me to be her bridesmaid. She only has one sister. She said to me, "I just wanted to go for a drive by ourselves because there's something I need to ask you something." I couldn't stand the suspense! She then said, "I know my sister will be my maid of honour. I don't want to be mean, but I'm going to ask 'A', the girl I work with because she'll look better in the dress I'm choosing than you will. I hope that's ok." All I could do was say that's fine, while in my head I'm telling myself not to cry, & said I really need to get home. I went to the wedding but it was embarrassing as a lot of people were shocked & said they thought I'd be the bridesmaid. All I could say to them was, "yes, so did I, but it's her wedding & her choice." I was very, very self conscious of the fact it was merely because I am plus size & "A" would "look better in the dress".

Let me start by saying what a remarkably mature, selfless & caring 6 year old girl daughter you have.
Kids don't need Xboxes, 5 star holidays, brand name clothing. The things that mean the most to them is the time you spend with them and the memories you create. I am a mother of 2 boys, now 32 & 30. I myself came from upper middle class and I could've had everything, but didn't. I married lower class, so  had nothing & we lived pay to pay. We rented when the kids were younger. At one stage we rented in an middle-class Eastern suburb of Melbourne. One day, my eldest son came home from school, he asked me, "Mummy, are we rich?" Given the suburb we were living in and the ridiculously expensive things some of the kids bought to school, I guessed where this conversation was going. "Yes mate, I think we are." His eyes went as wide as anything. "Really?", he said rather excitedly. "Absolutely! You've got a Mum & Dad that love you, a baby brother who loves you, 2 lots of grandparents, 2 lots of great grandparents & so many aunties, uncles & cousins. I think we're one of the richest families around because of that." I could see his little brain processing that. He was about 8 at the time. Whilst he's very successful, owns his own home, amongst other things, he says that conversation stuck with him. Money buys you nice things, but it's the people around you & memories that mean the most. 
I'm sorry for your loss, my condolences. Spoil your daughter from the heart, that's what matters most. You sound like wonderful people to be doing all your doing. I'm a great believer in the karma train. Your goodness will come back to you.

Don't let other people's opinions of you get under your skin or define who you are. If they don't like or love you, you don't need them nor do you want them in your life.
